Your leg day

Learn the movement. Then add the weight.

First, a little warm-up · 5 minutes

Walk or march for 3 minutes. Then practice 8 easy squats and 8 unweighted hip hinges. Take your time.

For each-leg exercises, log left and right reps, then check the set after both sides. Weight is the total you hold, or the ankle weight on each working leg. 0 lb = body weight.

A confident beginning

Your first steps to stronger.

Simple habits for learning the movements and building muscle over time.

Start small.

Use “First sessions” for one working set per exercise. After a few comfortable sessions, switch to two sets. The listed weights are trials, not targets you must reach.

This is one repeatable workout. Leave at least 48 hours before repeating it. Once a week is a starting point; a second session can help spread out practice and training as recovery allows.

Make progress measurable.

  1. Pick a weight that allows the bottom of the rep range with steady technique.
  2. Build reps while keeping 2–3 good reps in reserve.
  3. When every set reaches the top of the range for two workouts, add the smallest available weight increment.
  4. Return to the lower rep count. If the next weight is too heavy, stay with the current one.

Make the glutes do the work.

On bridges and donkey kicks, move from your hip without arching your back. On fire hydrants, lift the bent knee sideways only as far as your pelvis stays still.

Start without ankle weights. A 5 lb ankle weight can be a big jump. Never wedge a loose dumbbell behind the knee.

Support the growth.

Eat regular meals with enough food to support training, include a protein source at each meal, and prioritize sleep. Muscle gain takes consistent practice over months.

Rest about 90–120 seconds for the first three exercises and 60–90 seconds for the others. These are working sets, not a race or a timed circuit.

Exercise videos & training reference

Short demos link to their original publishers. U.S. Marine Corps / DVIDS: squat, Romanian deadlift, split squat, donkey kick. AFN Sasebo / DVIDS: fire hydrant. Sport Keele: glute bridge and calf raise. Follow this plan’s beginner adaptations rather than copying heavier demonstration loads.
